name: Boudica
occupation: Celtic queen who revolted against Rome
fact: Tacitus says she took poison rather than let Rome capture her — another historian says she just fell ill

name: Blackbeard
occupation: Notorious pirate killed off North Carolina
fact: He tucked lit, smoldering fuses under his hat before battle so smoke curled from his face like a demon

name: Christopher Marlowe
occupation: Playwright killed in a tavern brawl
fact: He was stabbed through the eye over a bar bill — by a man tied to the same spy network he worked for

name: Vlad the Impaler
occupation: Voivode of Wallachia with a taste for very public executions
fact: Ottoman envoys who refused to remove their turbans before him had them nailed to their skulls instead

name: Charles V
occupation: Holy Roman Emperor who abdicated to a monastery
fact: In retirement he grew obsessed with clockwork, joking that ruling nations was easier than syncing two clocks

name: Marco Polo
occupation: Venetian merchant and traveler
fact: His famous book was dictated from a prison cell in Genoa to a cellmate who was a professional romance writer

name: Ibn Battuta
occupation: Moroccan explorer and scholar
fact: He covered roughly 75,000 miles across three continents, some 60,000 more than Marco Polo ever managed

name: Xuanzang
occupation: Chinese Buddhist monk and pilgrim
fact: He left China for India in defiance of an imperial travel ban, dodging patrols and crossing deserts by night

name: Wu Zetian
occupation: The only woman to rule China as emperor in her own name
fact: She invented a handful of new Chinese characters, including one made just for her own name

name: Hongwu Emperor
occupation: Founder of the Ming dynasty
fact: The beggar turned emperor later purged tens of thousands of his own officials in paranoid, bloody sweeps

name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
occupation: Japanese warlord and unifier of Japan
fact: Born a foot soldier's son, he later stripped every peasant in Japan of the right to bear a sword

name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
occupation: Shogun who outwaited his rivals and won at Sekigahara
fact: A folk verse says that if the cuckoo won't sing, he'd simply wait — patience that outlasted two rival warlords

name: Shaka Zulu
occupation: Founder of the Zulu Kingdom
fact: Grieving his mother, he banned crop planting for a year and had thousands killed for showing too little sorrow

name: Chandragupta Maurya
occupation: Founder of the Maurya Empire
fact: He gave up his throne, became a Jain monk, and starved himself to death as an act of religious devotion

name: Aurangzeb
occupation: Mughal emperor who jailed his father and killed his brothers
fact: He had his rival brother's severed head delivered in a box to their imprisoned father as proof of victory

name: Bartolomeu Dias
occupation: Portuguese navigator who opened the sea road to the Indies

death.place: Cape of Good Hope, South Africa

fact: He named the cape he'd rounded 'Cape of Storms' — the king renamed it Good Hope to sell the voyage

name: Henry the Navigator
occupation: Portuguese prince and patron of exploration
fact: He never once sailed on a voyage of exploration himself — he just funded and sent others

name: El Cid
occupation: Castilian military leader
fact: The legendary Christian hero spent years as a mercenary defending Muslim Zaragoza from Christian armies

name: Ibn Khaldun
occupation: Arab historian and philosopher
fact: Besieged in Damascus, he had himself lowered over the city walls in a basket to negotiate with Tamerlane

name: Rumi
occupation: Persian poet and Sufi mystic
fact: Shams of Tabriz, the mystic who inspired him, vanished one night in 1247 and was never seen again

name: Averroes
occupation: Andalusian philosopher and jurist
fact: The caliph had his books burned and him exiled — Europe's Christian scholars are why any of it survived

name: Vasco Núñez de Balboa
occupation: Conquistador who first saw the Pacific from the Americas
fact: The discoverer of the Pacific was beheaded on false treason charges ordered by his own fiancée's father

name: Alexander Nevsky
occupation: Russian prince and military commander
fact: He refused an alliance with the pope, submitted to Mongol overlords instead — and got sainted for it

name: Themistocles
occupation: Athenian statesman and general
fact: He beat Persia at Salamis, then later defected there and died governing a city for the Persian king

name: Demosthenes
occupation: Athenian orator and statesman
fact: Cornered by Macedonian soldiers, he bit down on a poisoned pen rather than be taken alive

name: Ptolemy I Soter
occupation: Macedonian general and founder of Ptolemaic Egypt
fact: He hijacked Alexander the Great's funeral cortege mid-transit and stole the body for Egypt

name: Selim I
occupation: Sultan who doubled the empire and took the caliphate
fact: He conquered Egypt, the Levant and the holy cities in eight years, tripling Ottoman territory

name: Osman I
occupation: Founder of the Ottoman Empire
fact: Founding legend says he dreamed of a tree growing from his chest, its branches shading the whole world

name: Babur
occupation: Founder of the Mughal Empire
fact: The Mughal founder wept over a melon sent from home, saying India had nothing to compare

name: Willem Barentsz
occupation: Dutch navigator and explorer
fact: His crew wintered in a driftwood hut fighting off polar bears; he died as the ice finally released them

name: Afonso de Albuquerque
occupation: Portuguese admiral and viceroy of India
fact: He tried to blockade the Red Sea and starve Mecca's pilgrim trade — the first Christian fleet ever to try it

name: Nicolaus Copernicus
occupation: Canon who put the Sun at the centre
fact: He moonlighted as a monetary economist, and his treatise beat Gresham to Gresham's law by decades

name: Tycho Brahe
occupation: Danish astronomer
fact: He lost the bridge of his nose in a duel over who was the better mathematician, and wore a metal one after

name: Johannes Kepler
occupation: Astronomer and mathematician
fact: While charting the heavens, he spent years defending his own mother against a witchcraft charge

name: Guru Nanak
occupation: Founder of Sikhism
fact: Legend has him resting with feet toward Mecca's Kaaba — scolded, he said God has no single direction

name: Buddha
occupation: Founder of Buddhism
fact: He was sheltered from the world until 29 — one ride outside the palace showed him old age, sickness, death

name: Maimonides
occupation: Jewish philosopher and physician
fact: He spent his final decades as court physician to Saladin's family, philosophy squeezed in around house calls

name: William Tyndale
occupation: English Bible translator
fact: He coined the word 'scapegoat' for his English Bible — then was strangled and burned for translating it

name: Girolamo Savonarola
occupation: Italian friar and reformer
fact: He torched Florence's art and finery in the Piazza della Signoria — then was hanged and burned there himself

name: Huldrych Zwingli
occupation: Swiss Protestant reformer
fact: He died fighting at Kappel; his enemies quartered his body and burned it mixed with pig offal

name: Andreas Vesalius
occupation: Anatomist who cut up bodies to correct Galen
fact: Accused of dissecting a still-living man, sentenced to a Jerusalem pilgrimage — he died on the way back

name: Kamehameha I
occupation: First king of the Hawaiian Islands
fact: His bones were hidden by trusted allies after death and have never been found — by design

name: Piri Reis
occupation: Ottoman admiral and cartographer
fact: His 1513 map charted South America with eerie accuracy; decades later the Ottomans beheaded him anyway

name: Hayreddin Barbarossa
occupation: Corsair who became the Ottoman navy
fact: For centuries, no Ottoman fleet left Istanbul without firing a cannon salute at his tomb first

name: Yi Sun-sin
occupation: Korean admiral who never lost a battle at sea
fact: At Myeongnyang he held a strait against 133 Japanese warships with just 13 of his own — and won

name: Christine de Pizan
occupation: Medieval writer and poet
fact: Widowed with children to feed, she became Europe's first person to earn a living purely by writing

name: Yongle Emperor
occupation: Ming emperor who moved the capital and built the Forbidden City
fact: He built the Forbidden City and launched Zheng He's treasure fleet — ships dwarfing Columbus's

name: Bayezid I
occupation: Sultan whose empire nearly died with him in captivity
fact: Captured by Tamerlane at Ankara in 1402, he died in captivity within a year — cause still disputed

name: Roxelana
occupation: Ottoman empress consort
fact: A captured slave girl, she became the sultan's only legal wife — unheard of in Ottoman tradition

name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
occupation: Persian astronomer and mathematician
fact: His Mongol-funded observatory produced a geometric trick Copernicus may have borrowed centuries later

name: Francisco Vázquez de Coronado
occupation: Conquistador who crossed the southwest chasing golden cities
fact: He bankrupted himself chasing legendary cities of gold and found only mud-brick villages

name: Peter Abelard
occupation: French philosopher and theologian
fact: When her uncle learned of the affair, he sent men to castrate Abelard in his sleep

name: Guru Gobind Singh
occupation: Tenth Sikh Guru
fact: He founded the Khalsa warrior order, then died from a stab wound eight years later — the stitches reopened

name: Baldwin I of Jerusalem
occupation: First Crusader King of Jerusalem
fact: His own brother turned down the crown as blasphemous — Baldwin had no such qualms and took it

name: Simon de Montfort
variants: simon de montfort 6th earl of leicester
occupation: English nobleman and rebel leader
fact: The father of England's Parliament was killed at Evesham, then castrated and beheaded as a trophy

name: Toussaint Louverture
occupation: Leader of the Haitian Revolution
fact: He built an army of former slaves that beat Spanish, British, and Napoleon's own troops in turn

name: Giuseppe Mazzini
occupation: Italian nationalist revolutionary
fact: He fought decades for a united Italy, then watched it unify as a monarchy — the one thing he never wanted

name: Lajos Kossuth
occupation: Hungarian revolutionary statesman
fact: Exiled after 1848, he became the first foreigner since Lafayette to address the US Congress

name: José Martí
occupation: Cuban poet and independence leader
fact: Ordered to stay in the rear at Dos Ríos, he charged into Spanish fire instead and was killed instantly

name: Sun Yat-sen
occupation: Revolutionary and first president of the Republic of China
fact: Detained by China's London legation in 1896, he was freed only after smuggling word out to his old professor

name: Rosa Luxemburg
occupation: Revolutionary socialist theorist
fact: Shot and dumped in a Berlin canal by right-wing paramilitaries, her body wasn't found for five months

name: Wernher von Braun
occupation: Rocket engineer who worked for both Hitler and NASA
fact: The engineer behind the moon rocket had been a Nazi SS officer whose earlier rockets used slave labor

name: Hedy Lamarr
occupation: Actress and inventor
fact: The Hollywood actress co-invented the frequency-hopping tech that underpins WiFi and Bluetooth today

name: Diego Rivera
occupation: Mexican muralist who painted revolution on public walls
fact: He snuck a portrait of Lenin into a Rockefeller Center mural; the whole thing got chiseled off the wall

name: Paul Gauguin
occupation: Stockbroker who gave up finance for paint, and Europe for the tropics
fact: He abandoned his wife and five children for Tahiti, vowing to return rich — he died there broke instead

name: Igor Stravinsky
occupation: Composer whose ballet premiere started a riot in Paris
fact: The Rite of Spring's 1913 premiere caused fistfights and a hatpin stabbing in the Paris audience

name: Sergei Rachmaninoff
occupation: Composer and pianist with hands that could span twelve keys
fact: His hand could stretch the interval of a thirteenth on the keyboard — about twelve inches across

name: Joseph Conrad
occupation: Polish sea captain who became an English novelist
fact: English was his third language after Polish and French — he wrote some of its greatest prose in it

name: T. E. Lawrence
occupation: British officer who fought alongside the Arab Revolt
fact: His fatal motorcycle crash led directly to the surgeon's research that made crash helmets standard

name: Patrice Lumumba
occupation: First prime minister of the Congo

birth.place: Onalua, Democratic Republic of the Congo

death.place: Katanga, Democratic Republic of the Congo

fact: Belgian-backed killers dissolved his body in acid; decades later, Belgium returned his family a gold tooth

name: Anwar Sadat
occupation: Egyptian president assassinated at his own military parade
fact: Assassinated during his own Victory Day parade — the shooters had marched in it, then broke ranks to attack

name: Malcolm X
occupation: Nation of Islam minister who broke with it and was shot for it
fact: A 1964 pilgrimage to Mecca dissolved his belief that white people were inherently evil, he wrote

name: Amelia Earhart
occupation: American aviator, first woman to fly the Atlantic solo
fact: She set the women's world speed record in 1930, then flew solo across the Atlantic just two years later

name: Percy Fawcett
occupation: Explorer who vanished hunting a lost city in the Amazon
fact: His hunt for a lost Amazon city inspired Conan Doyle's The Lost World — then the jungle took him too

name: Robert Falcon Scott
occupation: Royal Navy officer and polar explorer
fact: He reached the South Pole only to find Amundsen's Norwegian flag already planted there, five weeks early

name: Josephine Baker
occupation: Entertainer and civil rights activist
fact: She spied for the French Resistance, smuggling troop movements in invisible ink on her sheet music

name: W. E. B. Du Bois
occupation: Sociologist and civil rights activist
fact: At 93, exiled by his own government's refusal to renew his passport, he became a citizen of Ghana instead

name: James Baldwin
occupation: American writer who argued with his country from Paris
fact: He moved to Paris at 24, saying he could finally see America clearly only from outside it

name: Subhas Chandra Bose
occupation: Indian nationalist leader
fact: He sought help from Hitler and Japan, then died in a plane crash so disputed many doubt it happened

name: Yitzhak Rabin
occupation: Israeli PM assassinated after signing peace accords
fact: He signed the Oslo peace accords, then was shot dead by a fellow Israeli who opposed them

name: Robert Koch
occupation: Doctor who identified the bacteria behind TB and cholera
fact: The man who identified tuberculosis left his wife for an art student thirty years his junior

name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
occupation: Philosopher who twice decided he'd finished philosophy
fact: He inherited one of Europe's largest fortunes, gave it all away, and became a village schoolteacher instead

name: Marc Chagall
occupation: Painter of floating lovers and Russian village dreams
fact: At 77, he painted the ceiling of the Paris Opera for free, just for the honor of doing it

name: Olaudah Equiano
occupation: Writer and abolitionist
fact: His memoir helped end Britain's slave trade — historians still debate if he was truly born in Africa

name: Louis Riel
occupation: Métis political leader
fact: After his first rebellion, he spent two years in an asylum under a fake name before leading a second one

name: Rudolf Nureyev
occupation: Ballet star who defected to the West at the height of the Cold War
fact: At a Paris airport in 1961, he broke from his Soviet handlers and threw himself at French police

name: Kwame Nkrumah
occupation: First president of Ghana
fact: Toppled while visiting China, he never went home — Guinea's president made him honorary co-president

name: Haile Selassie
occupation: Ethiopian emperor revered as a messiah in Jamaica
fact: In 1936 he told the League of Nations 'it is us today, it will be you tomorrow' — they ignored him

name: Nina Simone
occupation: Singer and civil rights activist
fact: Curtis Institute rejected the classical pianist she wanted to be; she blamed race and never let it go

name: Jimi Hendrix
occupation: Guitarist who turned feedback into a national anthem
fact: He joined the army to dodge prison time, then washed out of the 101st Airborne within about a year

name: Simon Wiesenthal
occupation: Nazi hunter and Holocaust survivor
fact: He tipped off Israeli agents to Eichmann's hideout in Argentina, kicking off the hunt that caught him

name: Marcus Garvey
occupation: Pan-Africanist political activist
fact: Convicted of mail fraud for a ship his company didn't yet own, he served two years then was deported

name: Golda Meir
occupation: Israel's first and only woman prime minister
fact: After Munich's 1972 massacre, she personally authorized Mossad's secret hit squads to hunt down the plotters

name: Alexander Solzhenitsyn
occupation: Novelist who survived the camps and then described them
fact: The Gulag Archipelago got him arrested and stripped of Soviet citizenship within weeks of publication

name: George Mallory
occupation: Climber who explained himself with 'because it is there'
fact: He vanished near Everest's summit in 1924; his body wasn't found until 1999, the mystery still unsolved

name: Isadora Duncan
occupation: Barefoot dancer strangled by her own scarf
fact: Her trademark flowing scarf caught in a car's rear wheel and strangled her instantly

name: Ayrton Senna
occupation: Brazilian driver of three world titles and one great rivalry
fact: He died with an Austrian flag tucked in his car, meant to honor a rival killed racing the day before

name: Idi Amin
occupation: Ugandan dictator who awarded himself every medal going
fact: His self-given titles included 'Conqueror of the British Empire' and 'Lord of All the Beasts of the Earth'

name: Bruce Lee
occupation: Martial artist and actor who brought kung fu to global screens
fact: He died at 32 from brain swelling; the exact trigger is still debated fifty years later

name: George Gershwin
occupation: Composer who married the concert hall to jazz
fact: The composer of Rhapsody in Blue died at 38 from a brain tumor doctors had dismissed as nerves

name: Lee Harvey Oswald
occupation: Assassin of John F. Kennedy
fact: Two days after killing Kennedy, he was shot dead himself on live television, in a police station basement

name: Anastasio Somoza Debayle
occupation: President and dictator of Nicaragua
fact: Exiled in Paraguay, he was killed by a bazooka round fired at his limousine from a nearby rooftop porch

name: Frantz Fanon
occupation: Psychiatrist and anti-colonial writer
fact: The anti-colonial thinker died of leukemia in a Maryland hospital, flown to America for treatment

name: Anna Pavlova
occupation: Ballerina with a dying-swan solo and a dessert named after her
fact: She refused surgery near the end — 'if I can't dance, I'd rather be dead,' she said

name: Erich Maria Remarque
occupation: German veteran whose war novel the Nazis burned
fact: The Nazis burned his anti-war novel, then executed his sister and billed the family for the guillotine

name: Benjamin Disraeli
occupation: Prime minister and novelist
fact: Born Jewish but baptized to enter politics, he bought Suez Canal shares on a Rothschild loan

name: Lord Beaverbrook
occupation: Press baron and wartime minister
fact: Churchill put him in charge of aircraft production — Dowding said no one else could have done it

name: Pedro II of Brazil
occupation: Brazil's long-reigning emperor, later deposed and exiled
fact: At an 1876 expo he was first to hear Bell's telephone speak, gasping: my god, it talks

name: Thomas Cochrane
occupation: Naval commander and liberator
fact: Convicted of stock fraud, he was pilloried and stripped of knighthood — restored by Victoria in 1847

name: Marquis de Lafayette
occupation: Revolutionary aristocrat
fact: He mailed George Washington the actual key to the Bastille; it still hangs at Mount Vernon

name: Samuel Baker
occupation: Victorian explorer who named Lake Albert
fact: He won his wife Florence by bribing her captors at an Ottoman slave auction on the Danube

name: Mary Kingsley
occupation: Victorian woman who explored West Africa in full skirts
fact: Her thick Victorian skirt saved her life, cushioning a fall onto a spiked animal trap

name: Roger Casement
occupation: Human-rights investigator and rebel
fact: Diaries detailing his sex life were leaked by British intelligence to sink his reprieve petition

name: Roger Williams
occupation: Religious dissenter and founder
note: Birth year is conventionally given as c.1603.
fact: Banished for dissent, he insisted on buying Providence's land from the Narragansett rather than take it

name: John Winthrop
occupation: Puritan governor who promised a city upon a hill
fact: Aboard the Arbella he preached the colony would be a city upon a hill, watched by all

name: William Penn
occupation: Quaker who founded a colony on religious tolerance
fact: The king insisted the colony carry the Penn name; the Quaker founder himself never wanted it

name: John Smith
occupation: Leader of the Jamestown colony
fact: Before Jamestown he was a slave in Istanbul who beat his master to death and fled on his horse

name: John Hanning Speke
occupation: Explorer who claimed the Nile's source and died before the argument ended
fact: He died in a shooting accident the day before his public showdown with Burton over the Nile

name: Richard Francis Burton
occupation: Explorer and linguist who translated forbidden books
fact: He snuck into Mecca in disguise, knowing discovery as a Christian meant instant death

name: Freya Stark
occupation: Travel writer who mapped remote corners of Arabia and Persia
fact: A factory machine tore off part of her scalp at thirteen; she wore flamboyant hats to hide the scars

name: Wilfred Thesiger
occupation: Explorer who twice crossed the Empty Quarter
fact: He despised the motor car, blaming engines for shrinking a world he loved wild

name: Gertrude Bell
occupation: Archaeologist and mapmaker of Iraq
fact: She scaled peaks across the Alps first; one summit in the Bernese Oberland still bears her name

name: Arthur Evans
occupation: Archaeologist of Knossos
fact: He rebuilt Knossos in concrete from his own imagination, inventing as much as he excavated

name: Mary Leakey
occupation: Archaeologist who found the Laetoli footprints
fact: She uncovered 3.6-million-year-old footprints at Laetoli, proof our ancestors walked upright

name: Louis Leakey
occupation: Anthropologist who pushed human origins back into Africa
fact: With no science degree himself, he handpicked Goodall, Fossey and Galdikas to study great apes

name: Abd el-Kader
occupation: Algerian resistance leader
fact: The Algerian who fought France for years sheltered thousands of Damascus Christians in his own home

name: Tewodros II
occupation: Ethiopian emperor who shot himself rather than be captured
fact: Cornered at Magdala, he shot himself with a pistol once gifted to him by Queen Victoria

name: Menelik II
occupation: Ethiopian emperor who crushed an Italian army at Adwa
fact: At Adwa in 1896 his army crushed an invading European power, the first to do so in the colonial age

name: Fridtjof Nansen
occupation: Polar scientist who later ran relief for refugees
fact: He invented a passport for the stateless, letting 450,000 refugees finally cross a border

name: John Franklin
occupation: Naval officer whose Arctic expedition vanished with all hands
fact: His lost crew left cut marks on their own bones, the last resort of men starving in the ice

name: Robert Peary
occupation: American who claimed the North Pole in 1909
fact: His own diary later cast doubt on whether he ever actually reached the pole he was credited with

name: Matthew Henson
occupation: African American explorer at the front of that Pole dash
fact: He likely stood at the North Pole before his commander, then waited decades for anyone to say so

name: John Reed
occupation: American journalist who reported a revolution from inside it
fact: The American radical is buried inside the Kremlin wall, one of only three of his countrymen so honored

name: Lafcadio Hearn
occupation: Writer and folklorist
fact: Blind in one eye, he became one of the first Westerners ever naturalized as a Japanese citizen

name: William Adams
occupation: Navigator and samurai retainer
fact: Shipwrecked in Japan, he became a samurai and the model for the hero of Shogun

name: Harald Hardrada
occupation: King of Norway and last great Viking warlord
fact: Before he was king he commanded the Byzantine emperor's Viking bodyguard in Sicily and beyond

name: David Livingstone
occupation: Missionary-explorer of Africa's rivers and lakes
fact: His heart was buried under an African tree; the rest of him sailed home to Westminster Abbey

name: Leif Erikson
occupation: Norse explorer who reached America five centuries before Columbus
fact: He earned the nickname Leif the Lucky not for finding Vinland but for rescuing shipwrecked sailors

name: Erik the Red
occupation: Exiled Norseman who founded Greenland's first settlement
fact: Exiled for manslaughter, he named a mostly-ice island Greenland purely to lure settlers there

name: Zenobia
occupation: Rebel queen who tore the Roman east away and ruled it herself
fact: Paraded through Rome in golden chains, she ended her days as a Roman society philosopher

name: Empress Matilda
occupation: Claimant to the English throne during the Anarchy
fact: She escaped a besieged castle by dressing in white and slipping across the frozen Thames

name: Alcibiades
occupation: Athenian general and serial turncoat
fact: His last assassins finally cornered him by torching his house rather than facing him with a blade

name: Frederick II Hohenstaufen
occupation: Holy Roman Emperor they called the Wonder of the World
fact: Excommunicated twice, he still talked his way into Jerusalem and kept Europe's first giraffe

name: Henry IV of France
occupation: French king who reckoned Paris well worth a Mass
fact: The king who wished every family a Sunday chicken was stabbed to death in his own stalled carriage

name: Louis XV of France
occupation: French king of 'after me, the deluge'
fact: The deluge he predicted arrived for him first — he died of smallpox, his body blackened by it

name: Louis Philippe I
occupation: France's last king, who dressed like a banker
fact: The last king of France fled the 1848 revolution by cab, traveling incognito as Mr Smith

name: Napoleon III
occupation: France's first president and its last emperor
fact: He escaped a French prison by walking out its gate disguised as a laborer carrying a plank

name: James I of England
occupation: First king of both England and Scotland
fact: He survived being blown up by gunpowder plotters, then wrote a treatise damning tobacco instead

name: James II of England
occupation: Catholic king toppled in the Glorious Revolution
fact: Fleeing his own kingdom, he chucked the Great Seal of England into the Thames on his way out

name: George I of Great Britain
occupation: German-speaking first Hanoverian king of Britain
fact: He locked his wife away for adultery in a country house for the last three decades of her life

name: George III
occupation: The king who lost America and, at the last, his mind
fact: In one mad spell, he tried to shake hands with an oak tree, mistaking it for the King of Prussia

name: Harold Godwinson
occupation: Last Anglo-Saxon king, killed defending his crown in 1066
fact: Norman chroniclers said he'd sworn on holy relics to back William, then took the crown himself

name: Richard II of England
occupation: Boy king deposed by his cousin and quietly starved to death
fact: At fourteen he rode alone into a rebel mob at Smithfield and talked them into going home

name: Alexander II of Russia
occupation: Tsar who freed the serfs, killed by a bomb
fact: He survived the first bomb, stepped out to help the wounded, and was killed by the second

name: Christina of Sweden
occupation: Queen who abdicated to live free in Rome
fact: She wore men's clothes and abdicated for Rome; she's one of only three women buried in St Peter's

name: Gustavus Adolphus
occupation: Swedish king who made Sweden a great power and died in battle
fact: Swallowed by smoke at Lutzen, he rode off from his own men and was shot dead within minutes

name: John III Sobieski
occupation: Polish king who broke the siege of Vienna
fact: After breaking the siege of Vienna he wrote the Pope one line: we came, we saw, God conquered

name: Matthias Corvinus
occupation: Renaissance king of Hungary and his black army
fact: His private library rivaled the Vatican's, until the Ottomans scattered it after Mohacs

name: Constantine XI Palaiologos
occupation: Last emperor of Byzantium, lost on the walls
fact: No one could ever identify his corpse, so Greek legend still waits for the marble emperor to wake

name: Tiberius
occupation: Rome's gloomy second emperor, brooding on Capri
fact: He had to be begged onto the throne, then complained it made him a miserable overworked slave

name: Claudius
occupation: The stammering emperor everyone underestimated
fact: He marched into Britain behind war elephants in 43 AD, awing the tribes into surrender

name: Commodus
occupation: Emperor who fancied himself a gladiator
fact: He renamed Rome after himself and rewrote every month of the calendar with his own titles

name: Septimius Severus
occupation: African-born emperor who died at York
fact: On his deathbed his advice to his warring sons was simple: enrich the soldiers, scorn everyone else

name: Julian the Apostate
occupation: Last pagan emperor of Rome
fact: He tried to rebuild the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem purely to needle the triumphant Christians

name: Leonidas I
occupation: Spartan king of the last-stand three hundred
fact: Told to surrender Spartan weapons, his reported answer was two words: come and take them

name: Cato the Younger
occupation: Stubborn republican who out-stubborned Caesar
fact: He stabbed himself, and when a doctor stitched him up, tore his own wound back open by hand

name: Vercingetorix
occupation: Gaulish chieftain who defied Caesar
fact: Caesar kept him alive in a cell for six years just to march him through Rome before killing him

name: Mithridates VI
occupation: Poison-proof king who was Rome's nightmare
fact: He'd spent a lifetime dosing himself against poison and, at the end, found he couldn't die by it

name: Pyrrhus of Epirus
occupation: King whose costly wins gave us the Pyrrhic victory
fact: Cornered in a street brawl at Argos, he was finally killed by an old woman's roof tile

name: Seleucus I Nicator
occupation: Cavalry officer who inherited Alexander's east
fact: He stamped his family's names on dozens of new cities, seeding an empire with Antiochs and Seleucias

name: Gaius Marius
occupation: Seven-time consul who remade Rome's legions
fact: Hiding from assassins in a swamp, he reportedly scared off his own executioner with one sentence

name: Crassus
occupation: Richest man in Rome, undone at Carrhae
fact: After he fell to the Parthians, legend says they mocked his greed by pouring him molten gold

name: Basil II
occupation: Byzantine emperor who broke Bulgaria for good
fact: After his victory he blinded thousands of prisoners, sparing one eye in every hundred to lead them home

name: Belisarius
occupation: Justinian's general who won back Rome
fact: Outnumbered ten to one, he took North Africa from the Vandals with a single cavalry charge

name: Nader Shah
occupation: Persian conqueror who sacked Delhi for its jewels
fact: He stripped Delhi of its Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor, then waived taxes at home for three years

name: Shah Abbas I
occupation: Safavid shah who made Isfahan half the world
fact: He marched an entire Armenian trading town to Isfahan just to seize its silk network intact

name: Klemens von Metternich
occupation: Arch-conservative who redrew Europe at Vienna
fact: His empire's post was cheaper and faster than rivals' for one reason: he was steaming open the mail

name: Talleyrand
occupation: The limping bishop who served every French regime
fact: An excommunicated bishop, he served every French regime and joked that treason was a matter of timing

name: Cardinal Richelieu
occupation: Red-robed cardinal who really ran France
fact: The cardinal who ran France also founded the Academie francaise to police the French language

name: William Gladstone
occupation: Victorian PM four times over, ever more radical with age
fact: The four-time premier spent his nights walking London's streets trying to reform prostitutes

name: Robert Peel
occupation: PM who gave Britain its first police force
fact: The man who gave London its police force died after a skittish new horse threw and then trampled him

name: William Wilberforce
occupation: MP who fought to abolish the slave trade
fact: He died three days after hearing that slavery's abolition in the empire was finally secured

name: Camillo Cavour
occupation: Cunning architect of a united Italy
fact: The architect of a united Italy died months after the crown he built, before Rome ever joined it

name: Georges Clemenceau
occupation: French wartime premier who saw the Great War through
fact: In his fifties he fought a pistol duel over a scandal; both men emptied their guns and missed

name: Konrad Adenauer
occupation: West Germany's steady first chancellor
fact: The Gestapo jailed him after the plot on Hitler's life; four years later, aged 73, he became chancellor

name: Josip Broz Tito
occupation: Partisan who ruled Yugoslavia entirely his own way
fact: His private train carried him to an island retreat where he hosted Elizabeth Taylor and the Queen

name: Robert E. Lee
occupation: Confederate general in the American Civil War
fact: A Union general seeded his lawn with war dead on purpose, turning it into Arlington National Cemetery

name: Stonewall Jackson
occupation: Confederate general who stood like a stone wall
fact: He rode into battle with one arm raised skyward, convinced it kept his body's blood in balance

name: Duke of Marlborough
occupation: Unbeaten general who won the day at Blenheim
fact: Early in his career he spent five weeks in the Tower of London on a forged charge of treason

name: Prince Eugene of Savoy
occupation: Austria's greatest general against the Turks
fact: Louis XIV sneered at his looks and refused him a French commission; Austria took him instead and won

name: Alexander Suvorov
occupation: Russian general who never once lost a battle
fact: Trapped in the Alps, he led his army out through snow so deep that half of it never emerged

name: Mikhail Kutuzov
occupation: One-eyed general who bled Napoleon white in 1812
fact: He took a bullet clean through the skull near one eye, survived, then took a second in nearly the same spot

name: Michel Ney
occupation: Napoleon's marshal, the bravest of the brave
fact: He'd sworn to bring Napoleon back in an iron cage, then joined him instead; the firing squad came for that
